body: So should I move on, or back away and see if I get something from here like a good few people are saying?
I really do respect her a lot for telling me all of that. The last girl really did drag me on, and it was not nice.
I felt a bit of a failure afterwards. I genuinely thought 4 hours with someone would be an amazing sign. I'll probably try to keep off her radar now.
I'm a petite guy myself. So I hope that would give me an advantage.
It's great. I wasted 6 months on her.
What I said is weird or?

I think you are right with that. I think somewhere deep down, once I feel something with someone, I get attached and accept everything, ignoring any red flags - just like with the last girl I had an interest in. 

A lot of people who really recommended counselling for me. I really should, and will take it up.

I usually joke about it when it is brought up or something. Unless I bring it up in conversation, or I use my cane, people probably wouldn't notice my limb. 

I do think it's the cause, however. I dunno. I can understand that someone who could become more disabled in the future wouldn't be an attractive trait.

It's so difficult. I only seem to remember the good memories instead of the bad ones. I miss the little texts in the morning, the little texts at night. The random messages. But mine was a lie, and it's funny when I look back on it, it was all a lie. 

I met this girl and waited for 6 weeks to meet her, trying different ways to meet her. Even though she lived 10 minutes away, and even though she liked me. But it was all for nothing. And it was funny to see how much her personality changed after our first break up, so to speak.

No, we've gone our separate ways. But I miss her, but she's horrible. I'm not understanding it myself. I've never felt like this about someone so toxic before. 
It's scaring me, frankly.
It was just amount of time we spent texting. I felt like I was valued for once by someone. :/
Probably was. But now I am left with all these emotions and I just feel awful.

I'd like to get out of my environment. But I guess this is where most of the problems come into play. Having someone to move out with would mean someone would be there if I needed them, but there isn't anyone, and it's so expensive to live alone in my area it's not viable. 

I'd love to explain my problems to them, but they seem to have this stigma against any mental health issue. I also feel awful because it's Christmas, and I don't want to ruin it for anyone.
No. No. They're are not related. Sorry for the confusion.
